playbook.disclaimer: Template only. Follow your utility's own emergency response plan and your state's rules. This checklist gives no regulatory advice.

steps.text: Read the physical pressure gauge and the tank sight glass at the site and enter both readings.
Check the Witness Node lights at the pump and compare them with what the screen says.
Call a second person and tell them what you see.
Take internet-exposed controllers and remote access off the network, following the utility's own plan.
Switch to manual operation where it is safe to do so.

steps.target: when 50% of the clock is left
steps.text: Send a crew to the pump station and alert the manager.

steps.target: when 50% of the clock is left
steps.text: Contact the state drinking-water program, as your plan requires.

steps.target: when 25% of the clock is left
steps.text: Prepare the precautionary notice, as your plan requires.
Verify equipment state physically before restoring remote control.
Record the sequence: export the evidence log and verify its chain.

scenarios.name: Frozen screen (PLC lockout)
scenarios.summary: Attackers lock the operator out and the screen stops updating. Then the pump quietly stops.

scenarios.name: Pumps forced off behind a careful forgery
scenarios.summary: The screen looks alive, noisy and self-consistent, and says Pump 2 is running. It was forced off.

scenarios.name: Alarms off, remote access cut, pump cycles changed
scenarios.summary: Modeled on the late-August Colorado reports: the screen goes dark while pumps are cycled.

scenarios.name: Replayed data
scenarios.summary: The screen replays recorded normal data from 30 minutes earlier while Pump 2 is stopped.

scenarios.name: Valve closed out of sight
scenarios.summary: A main valve is closed and the screen is forged. Only customers notice. The node can't see this.

scenarios.name: Power outage that looks like an attack
scenarios.summary: Mains power fails: pumps stop, SCADA goes dark, the node runs on backup power. Attack or outage?
